proposed_features.description: The primary alignment of the swimmer's body relative to the water surface, which distinguishes horizontal swimming from vertical falling.
The specific kinematic cycle of the arms, distinguishing the alternating overhand motion from the simultaneous symmetrical motion or the lack of swimming strokes.
The type of leg propulsion used, distinguishing the continuous flutter kick from the whip-like kick or the lack of swimming kicks.
The position of the head relative to the water surface, which is a key differentiator between the two swimming styles and the diving actions.
The temporal length of the primary action, distinguishing the continuous, repetitive nature of swimming from the short, transient nature of diving.
The location of the subject at the beginning of the clip, distinguishing actions starting from a platform or cliff versus those starting in the water.
The physical setting of the activity, which helps distinguish indoor pools, outdoor pools, and natural rock formations.
The visibility of lane ropes or lines, which are characteristic of competitive or training pools but absent in natural settings.
The occurrence of a large, singular water disturbance, which is a hallmark of the entry phase of diving.
The path of the subject through the scene, distinguishing linear horizontal movement from vertical descent.
The visibility of a springboard or diving platform, which is specific to the diving category.
The presence of other people watching the action, which is common in pool settings but rare in natural cliff diving.
